purpose: Binding terminology + register decisions for every pt-BR translation agent. Parallel agents cannot see each other's work; this file is what keeps 631 UI keys, 2065 lesson units and ~107k words of prose consistent. Every translator reads it before starting; every QA reviewer audits against it.

register.address: você — informal, warm, direct. Never tu. Never o senhor / a senhora except inside a Korean service-desk roleplay where the Korean itself is formal.
register.imperatives: Use the você imperative ('Comece', 'Escolha', 'Ouça'), not the tu imperative ('Começa', 'Escolhe').
register.tone: Friendly teacher explaining to an adult beginner. Not academic, not childish, not marketing-hype.
register.gender: Prefer gender-neutral phrasing for the learner where natural ('quem aprende', 'estudantes'). Do NOT use @ or x endings — they read as web-forum style and break screen readers.
register.variety: Brazilian, not European. Concretely: 'usuário' not 'utilizador', 'tela' not 'ecrã', 'time' not 'equipa', 'celular' not 'telemóvel', 'ônibus' not 'autocarro', 'trem' not 'comboio', 'café da manhã' not 'pequeno-almoço', gerund ('está aprendendo') not 'está a aprender'.

never_translate.korean: All Hangul (한글, 한복, 삼겹살 …) stays exactly as written. Never transliterate it into Latin, never translate it away.
never_translate.kr_trans_blocks:
Any
…
is a Korean gloss — leave the whole block untouched.
never_translate.romanization: Revised Romanization in parentheses or in .rom-line / .rom-text / .rom-cell / .phrase-rom / .food-card-rom / .bap-rom nodes — identical in every locale by design.
never_translate.note_on_brands: Band, drama, film, agency, chef, restaurant and product names stay in their established Latin or Korean form. When unsure whether a term is a kept brand, check what culture/es/kbeauty.html did — if Spanish kept it in English, keep it.

place_names.rule: Use the established Portuguese exonym where one genuinely exists; otherwise keep the Latin transliteration unchanged.

domain_terms._note: Added 2026-08-13 after the learn-shell pass — terms the translators had to choose because they were not here. Recurring across pages, so they must be fixed.
domain_terms._kept_english: Tool names kept as English loanwords — verified es and de do the same: Flashcards, Browser, Quiz, min (abbreviation).

numbers_and_dates.currency_note: Korean won stays ₩ with the Brazilian separator (₩80.000). Do NOT convert prices to reais — they are facts about Korea, not offers to the reader.
numbers_and_dates.hangul_guard: ⚠️ Numbers sitting inside Korean text ('3,000만 개 이상') use the KOREAN comma convention and must NOT be reformatted. scripts/fix-locale-number-format.cjs enforces this; do not hand-edit those.

typography.quotes: Use “ ” for quoted speech. Do not use straight ASCII quotes in prose.
typography.ellipsis: Keep the source's … character rather than three periods.
typography.no_space_before_colon: Unlike French, Portuguese takes NO space before : ; ! ?
typography.entities: Leave & ' " intact — never decode them into raw characters.

hard_rules: Only ever ADD _pt_br fields to learn/data/*.json. Never modify the base/English field or another locale's field.
choices / rules arrays are ORDER-LOAD-BEARING — the quiz answer is matched by index. Preserve length and order exactly.
An all-Korean choices array must have NO choices_pt_br copy at all. Hangul is Hangul in every locale; a per-locale copy both drifts and leaks the answer.
Keep {placeholders}, \n breaks and emoji exactly as in the source.
Never translate a lesson's Korean example into Portuguese in place of the Korean — translate only the surrounding explanation.
Do not weaken a grammar explanation to make it read more smoothly. A mistranslated grammar point is a worse defect than an untranslated one.

pronunciation_aid.decision: NONE. pt-BR is Latin-script and uses the shared Revised-Romanization line already present on every page. Do not invent a reading_pt_br field.
pronunciation_aid.registry: scripts/_locales.cjs pt-br.pronField === null — keep it that way.
